hints: The car of mass $1600\text{ kg}$ travels uphill at constant speed $32\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a slope with $\sin\theta = 0.08$. Constant resistance is $240\text{ N}$.
Since speed is constant ($a = 0$), the driving force balances resistance plus the component of weight down the slope: $F_D = 240 + 1600(10)(0.08)$.
Use $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to calculate power.
walkthrough:
Equate driving force to opposing forces for constant speed uphill:
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\theta = 240 + 1600(10)(0.08) = 240 + 1280 = 1520\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power output at $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = F_D \times v = 1520 \times 32 = 48640\text{ W}$$

walkthrough:
Calculate the reduced power ($95\%$ of original):
$$P_{\text{new}} = 0.95 \times 48640 = 46208\text{ W}$$

Find the driving force at speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{46208}{24} = 1925.33\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the slope:
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = ma$$
$$1925.33 - 240 - 1280 = 1600a$$
$$1925.33 - 1520 = 1600a$$
$$405.33 = 1600a \implies a = \frac{405.33}{1600} \approx 0.253\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Calculate the reduced engine power.

The power is decreased by $5\%$, meaning $95\%$ remains:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 0.95 \times 48640 = 46208\text{ W}$$

Step 2: Determine the driving force $F_D$ at speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{46208}{24} = \frac{5776}{3} \approx 1925.33\text{ N}$$
Step 3: Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ parallel to the slope.

The net force uphill is the driving force minus resistance and the downhill weight component:
$$F_D - (R + mg\sin\theta) = ma$$
$$\frac{5776}{3} - 1520 = 1600a$$
$$\frac{5776 - 4560}{3} = 1600a$$
$$\frac{1216}{3} = 1600a$$

Divide both sides by 1600:
$$a = \frac{1216}{4800} = \frac{19}{75} \approx 0.25333 \approx 0.253\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Therefore, the acceleration of the car at this instant is $0.253\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
